prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a highly refined, surprising but extremely minimal 8x Social website SECTION design. This is the next passage of one continuous warm-stone website, not a new hero. The first reference is the REAL 8x dashboard screenshot: use its data and product structure for credibility, NOT its blue palette, browser chrome, noisy cards or sidebar. The second reference is the currently approved page style: preserve stone #e9e5dc, ink #111111 and orange #f34b32, same gutters and restrained raster dots. DO NOT repeat the portrait or platform icon row.

Generate a finished flat desktop website screenshot, landscape 1600x1100. Aesthetic: contemporary Swiss editorial meets a beautifully considered software instrument. Sophisticated precision, calm hierarchy, unusually deliberate composition; no generic SaaS bento cards, no templates, no full-screen scene effect.

LAYOUT: ONE continuous solid stone background with 80px page margins. Top y50 is one fine horizontal black rule at 20% opacity. Heading across the upper-left at x80 y145, exact “The whole picture.” in tightly kerned modern grotesk, 76px, medium-semibold weight. Only the terminal dot is orange. At upper-right x1000 y165 an understated two-line sentence in23px: “Your creators, content and performance. In one place.” Keep a lot of useful open space, no paragraphs.

Below, around y330, build a single enormous open editorial PRODUCT CANVAS, nearly full width, so it is integrated INTO THE PAGE rather than a screenshot floating on top of it. No outer rounded rectangle, no browser top bar, no thick dark panel, no shadow, no white card surface. Keep the same stone background. Top row: simple horizontal text tabs “Overview” “Creators” “Content”, active Overview with a tiny orange dot and hairline underline. Small quiet right-aligned label “Product preview”. Thin horizontal separator beneath. These are local controls, not a new nav bar.

Within this canvas, left two-thirds is a stunning large field of precisely aligned tiny dots that doubles as a performance plot, a restrained stepped rising skyline drawn from dots. Geometry: 28 vertical columns of circular dots, all on an 8px grid, each column rises in a different restrained height from one shared baseline. The earliest columns are short, central moderately high, last five longest; the final column uses orange dots, all preceding columns ink. NO grid boxes, connecting lines, axes, floating data cards, made-up percentages or giant fake metrics. A small simple label above this plot says “Performance overview”; directly beneath it the words “Illustrative trend” in quiet readable13px so the chart cannot be mistaken for measured customer data. The dots are the unmistakable 8x brand language, and now serve a concrete information purpose. Beautiful mathematical spacing, sparse empty space over the graph, crisp raster marks, not a fan or ribbon or wave or particles or DNA. This flat dot chart occupies about x80–960, y470–870. It should feel elegant and editorial, not science-fiction or corporate infographic.

RIGHT THIRD x1080–1480 is a beautiful, sparse typography-led vertical product summary separated from the chart by just one hairline vertical rule, no boxes. Use ONLY these three actual values from the supplied product reference: “140.1K” with the small label “Users”; “120.6K” with label “Creators”; “265” with label “Videos”. Three rows, thin grey rules, precise right alignment of the numbers, generous spacing. Numbers are 40px, labels16px. These are explicitly under Product preview, not marketing claims. No percent increases, no invented client names, no extra KPIs.

Below the whole shared canvas y940, a thin baseline rule. Left side text link “Explore the platform” and a delicate diagonal arrow. Right side just three subdued words separated by middle dots “Track · Review · Learn”. Keep the final 80px stone and open. NO footer, map, pricing, testimonials, faces, repetitive photos, new decorative logo, or huge call-to-action button.

The image must look visually resolved and genuinely premium. The dot chart is ONE dominant focal visual with a clear product meaning. All content is grounded in the original 8x product's overview/creators/content functions. The small illustrative-trend label is required. Source values must be exact. The future orange map is not part of this frame; this section stays on stone and the document continues below. Natural page flow, quiet horizontal rules, one shared canvas with local selection, no page takeover.
